newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-New South Wales re-enters sugar export market.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-New South Wales re-enters sugar export market.

text.p: The Australian state of New South Wales (NSW) re-entered the direct raw sugar export market this month with a shipment to Singapore, the Australian Cane Farmers Association said in its Australian Sugar Digest.

The shipment of 21,500 tonnes through Brisbane on the MV Cherry Flower signalled the re-entry of the NSW Sugar Milling Co-operative to the raw sugar export market after an absence of eight years, it said. Australian sugar is traditionally exported by Queensland Sugar Corp, with about 95 percent of Australia's sugar produced in the state of Queensland.
General manager of the NSW Co-operative Greg Messiter said the decision to re-enter the export market followed a bumper year for raw sugar production in NSW.
NSW produced a record 285,000 tonnes of raw sugar in 1996, ten percent better than its previous best in 1994, he said.
"We expect that these crop levels will be maintained enabling us to continue to service export markets in the Asia-Pacific region," he said.
The contract to handle the shipment was awarded to Globex International Pty Ltd, the fully-owned bulk commodity handling ports subsidiary of Queensland co-operative Grainco Ltd.
Globex had invested more than A$200,000 in capital works converting a former grain shed into a fully-integrated, wharf-to-compound sugar storage facility at its Pinkenba terminal, he said.
In a seven-day-a-week operation, truck loads of the sugar were stockpiled at the new facility throughout September/October from Condong Mill to await shipment, he said.
Australian raw sugar production rose to 5.4 million tonnes net titre in 1996 from 5.0 million in 1995, according to figures released on Thursday by the Australian Sugar Milling Council.
